description: Two chains A close to B close to C where A and C differ. Complete linkage never proposes A with C. In the first chain every step changes meaning; in the second A and B are paraphrases and C widens the population.

inputs.statement: Speed bumps should be added on Main Street.

evidence.quote: just put speed bumps on Main Street

inputs.statement: Traffic calming measures should be added on Main Street.

evidence.quote: Main Street needs something to calm the traffic

inputs.statement: Traffic calming measures should be added across the whole district.

evidence.quote: calm the traffic in the whole district, not one street

inputs.statement: Bus travel should be free for people over 65.

evidence.quote: the bus should be free once you are over 65

inputs.statement: People over 65 should be able to ride the bus for free.

evidence.quote: let the over 65s ride the bus for free

inputs.statement: Bus travel should be free for everyone.

evidence.quote: make the bus free for everybody

must_not_merge.why: The chain's ends: one street and one measure versus the whole district.
One specific measure versus traffic calming in general.
One street versus the whole district.
The chain's ends: over 65 versus everyone.
